answer: A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, and hence the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 210 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. The zenith detector writes to island, and zephyr shows every merge. Submissions that land within 136 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 35 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
